savory seasoning.reason: the renamed 'umami' category: bouillon, fish sauce, miso, worcestershire and similar; a kind of food, where umami is a taste

juice.reason: fruit and vegetable juices and nectars (apple, pineapple, tomato, cranberry); citrus juices stay with citrus because the sour slots read that category

wine.reason: still, sparkling and fortified wine, sake, mirin and cooking wine; vermouth stays in liqueur

beer.reason: beer, ale, stout, lager and cider (ginger beer is a mixer; apple cider is a juice)

neutral.reason: contributes no taste of its own: water, ice, plain starch (flour, rice, bread, pasta), neutral spirit; stands alone in a label and feeds no taste axis

rich.reason: a fatty or creamy mouthfeel that is not one of the basic tastes (butter, oil, cream, egg yolk, avocado, nuts); a mouthfeel note, not a taste, so it feeds no taste axis; may lead a label with a taste after it (cream is 'rich sweet')
